record.original_question: A positive integer n is perfect when the sum of all its positive divisors equals 2n. Are there any odd perfect numbers?

evidence.quote: A positive integer n is said to be perfect if the sum of its positive divisors is equal to twice the number. Are there odd perfect numbers?

artifact.self_contained_problem: For a positive integer $n$, let $\sigma(n) = \sum_{d \mid n,\, d > 0} d$ denote the sum of its positive divisors. A positive integer $n$ is called perfect if $\sigma(n) = 2n$. Determine whether there exists an odd positive integer $n$ that is perfect, or prove that no such integer exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The existence of odd perfect numbers is a famous long-standing open problem in number theory. No odd perfect number is known, and known results only provide lower bounds (e.g., any odd perfect number must exceed $10^{1500}$) and structural constraints, but no proof of existence or non-existence has been established.

status_evidence.title: Perfect number - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: It is not known whether any odd perfect numbers exist; various results have been obtained, but none has helped to locate one or otherwise resolve the question of their existence.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of odd perfect numbers remains open.

status_evidence.title: Ochem & Rao, Odd perfect numbers are greater than 10^1500
status_evidence.snippet: We show that any odd perfect number is greater than 10^1500.
status_evidence.claim: Only lower bounds and constraints are known; existence question is unresolved.
